title: Operational Task Mesh: integrate lightweight admin microservices for safe oncall actions
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build an Operational Task Mesh (OTM) and lightweight admin utility microservices that let support and oncall engineers run small, auditable, idempotent operations as first-class tasks. This ticket covers: a typed task contract, an event-driven router that enqueues and dispatches tasks, RBAC + policy gating for dangerous actions, safe dry-run and preview mode, audit log / trace integration, and minimal SDK hooks so product teams can expose safe shortflows in the Console. Goal: reduce mean time to remediate (MTTR) for common support scenarios while preserving security and observability.
acceptance_criteria: OTM prototype deployed to staging that can route and execute 3 example admin microservices (clear-cache, restart-worker, rotate-key) via the new task contract
Task executions record structured audit events (actor, task id, inputs, result, duration) to the internal audit stream and show up in the Console tracing panel
RBAC checks are enforced for each task invocation and policy gating can block risky tasks unless canary group membership is granted
Dry-run mode returns a plausible plan and cost estimate without making state changes
SDK bindings (node/python) for enqueueing tasks documented and integrated into 1 internal product repo
End-to-end failure/retry semantics implemented with idempotency tokens; at-least-once retries do not cause duplicate side effects for provided examples
Performance: median enqueue-to-complete for simple tasks <= 800ms in staging under 95th percentile load generated in the harness
tasks: Design typed task contract and schema (inputs, outputs, idempotency_token, policy_tags)
Implement Task Router service (HTTP + pub/sub hook) with queue and backoff policy
Build three admin microservices: clear-cache, restart-worker, rotate-key (staging-only initially)
Integrate RBAC + policy engine and a canary membership check for high-risk tasks
Wire audit events to internal audit-stream and add Console trace visualization
Create node/python SDK samples and a small quickstart guide
Add dry-run/preview implementation and cost estimation for tokenized tasks
Construct end-to-end test harness & chaos tests for retry semantics
Run security review and record mitigations
Prepare rollout plan: staging -> limited canary -> org-wide
